correctness.rationale: The established two-point spherical Blaschke--Petkantschin formula has exact \(|\sin(u-v)|\) Jacobian and the \(4\pi\) area normalization. Great-circle intersections are two opposite arcs of length \(L=2\arcsin(\sin\theta/\sin i)\); a minimizing arc escapes exactly for cross-component pairs. Both ordered crosses contribute \(4(L-\sin L)\). Parameter differentiation evaluates the resulting integral to \(\pi\cos\theta(1-\cos\theta)\), proving \(P(\theta)=\cos\theta/[2(1+\cos\theta)]\). Direct numerical great-circle quadrature and an independent exact-max-latitude simulation check the factors without replacing the general proof.

value.rationale: The complete exact law is a motivated probability measure of geodesic nonconvexity for all symmetric spherical zones. Strict monotonicity and the unexpectedly nonzero thin-zone escape limit \(1/4\) against zero for the limiting equator demonstrate a singular boundary regime; the opposite full-sphere limit has linear decay. This is a natural all-parameter classification, not an arbitrary table value.
